newsitem.title: USA: Global Pacific Minerals proceeds with Chinese mine.
newsitem.headline: Global Pacific Minerals proceeds with Chinese mine.

text.p: Canadian mining company, Global Pacific Minerals Inc said China had approved the company's plan to produce copper, gold, iron and cobalt from the Qian Chang skarn deposit in Anhui Province.
Local mining engineering firms are preparing to de-water the mine's twin shafts and underground workings, and some $440,000 will be spent to firm up reserves over nine months.
"The deposit will then be put into production at a rate of 330,000 tonnes per year at an estimated capital cost of about US$6 million within 1.5 years," Global said in a statement.

Anticipated annual production from the mine is 5.1 million pounds of copper, 21,000 ounces of gold, 229,000 tonnes of iron concentrates containing 64 percent iron, and 64,710 pounds of cobalt at a cash cost of US$22 per tonne of ore.
